items.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2024 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: So I can look at a basketball player, say like a guy like Michael Jordan for instance

ctx.x: Yeah I think it applies to everything. So what I mean by that is — I was reading something about Beethoven, like a kind of biographical thing. And he made a statement that was curious. And he said, “If you know the secret of correspondence you can do anything.” And I think I understood what that meant, and that’s kind of what Barry meant. And I see what it means now. And basically when you say looking at dance, looking at art, if you’re able to look at anything and see how it corresponds to any other

thing, no matter what the construct is, no matter what the medium through which a particular behavior is being — it doesn’t make any difference. You see the — you see the correspondence between the two supposedly different constructs. But the behavior — you can see it. So then you become — you understand the DNA of metaphor and the DNA of analogy — analogists. You can see the thing. And the only difference is the mediums through which particular things are being expressed, but it’s still being expressed by human…

Marvelous. I wonder if you’ve ever had a circumstance where you were the elder musician with wisdom and, much like Barry Harris, and you tried to pass that on to younger musicians who might have been on a very narrow path?
